title: Observe Pi's interactive /login flow, and what the same launch does without a TTY
statement: Establish, against the pinned runtime and with nothing of Kiln's involved, what Pi's interactive login does. Pi 0.84.4 has no authentication-only launch: `pi auth` offers only `check`, `print-api-key` and `print-bearer-token`, and `/login` exists only as a slash command inside the interactive TUI. The manual check therefore launches the full interactive Pi TUI against an isolated Pi configuration, types `/login`, takes the built-in `openai` API-key route with a throwaway key, exits, and then checks auth state separately with `pi auth check --provider openai --json --no-refresh` rather than inferring it from the exit code. It records whether the TUI owns the terminal while this runs. That check confirms locally configured authentication only and does not prove the key works against a provider. The no-TTY controls keep the launch arguments fixed and vary stdin and stdout. Each records which mode Pi selected and a bounded outcome: its exit and code, an error, or still running at a stated timeout. They are not the interactive mode and are not described as it. A sanitized transcript is retained, and the entered key is never recorded. Real subscription OAuth and proof of usable account authentication belong to TSK-0066.
notes: ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-03 TO PI'S BEHAVIOUR ALONE. The original wording mixed an observation of the runtime with a requirement on Kiln's wrapper, and its criterion demanded a Kiln recovery message — which cannot exist before the setup command does. What Kiln must DO about the no-TTY case is now its own task against the setup component. ⚠️ THE OBSERVATION RECORDS WHAT PI DOES; IT DOES NOT DECIDE WHETHER SETUP NEEDS ITS CHECK. Pi selects print mode when either stream is redirected, so setup needs its TTY check to reach /login at all (F8). What this measures is the bounded outcome of those print-mode runs, which tells setup what an unguarded launch would have done. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-09-21 (F7, F8). The earlier wording asked for an 'authentication-only step', which Pi 0.84.4 does not have (F7). And Pi selects print mode whenever stdin or stdout is not a TTY (resolveAppMode in dist/main.js), so a no-TTY run of the same arguments is a different mode rather than the same interactive one without a terminal; with stdin a pipe, Pi also reads it until it closes (F8). The route is the built-in openai API-key login with a throwaway key, because it exercises /login without an account.
